players.product: infrared and visible optical components, Black Diamond infrared glass (used instead of germanium), assemblies and modules, and infrared cameras

quarterly_data.signal: LightPath's 10-K revenue by shipping destination for fiscal 2026 (year ended June 30, 2026): United States $37,040,332 (fiscal 2025: $22,956,327); United Kingdom $14,998,206 ($3,434,525) - the majority of UK shipments are for a customer that integrates products in the UK and returns them to its customers in the U.S.; Israel $7,700,312 ($2,700,537); China $4,524,750 ($2,912,179); other European countries $4,652,974. Sales outside the U.S. were 48% of net revenue versus 38% in fiscal 2025, with Europe and Asia 97% of foreign sales; the 10-K notes that one of its largest customers integrates products in Europe and ships to U.S. customers, so true international sales are lower.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026: United States $37,040,332; United Kingdom $14,998,206; Israel $7,700,312; China $4,524,750; 48% outside the U.S. (38% in FY2025)

quarterly_data.signal: LightPath's 10-K on supply and capacity: fiscal 2026 capital expenditures (approximately $6.3 million) were primarily for expansion of glass fabrication capacity plus metrology and infrared coating equipment; fiscal 2026 working-capital investment of $9.6 million was driven by receivables and inventory and by supplier prepayments for critical materials with long lead times. The company states that it is estimated that over 60% of the global Germanium supply originates from China and that restrictions on supply from Russia and China raised Germanium prices from around $1,000 per Kg a few years ago to over $6,000 per Kg today, while its BlackDiamond glasses (including materials exclusively licensed from the U.S. Naval Research Laboratory since December 2021; BDNL-4 introduced April 2024) are made in the USA from raw ingredients available from many countries. After the sale of the China subsidiary (LPOIZ, expected to close in September 2026) LightPath expects to depend more on third-party suppliers, including LPOIZ's new owners.
quarterly_data.figure: Germanium from around $1,000 per Kg to over $6,000 per Kg; over 60% of supply from China; FY2026 working-capital investment $9.6 million
